name: Observability: logs, metrics, and traces from one signal model
purpose: Owns the three telemetry signals as one coherent model: structured JSON logs, RED metrics with per-class and probe series, and OpenTelemetry-compatible traces, all keyed by the same request id and auth class so any signal pivots to the others.
responsibilities: Emit structured JSON log lines with the base fields, request id, trace id, and per-class completion levels (rest-REQ-012, rest-US-2114).
Record RED metrics per path template and method, per-class counters, duration histograms, and the dedicated probe-outcome series (rest-US-2115).
Produce server spans per request with the declared attributes, honour inbound traceparent, and propagate context to downstream calls (rest-US-2116).
Apply the redaction rules before any signal leaves the process: no secrets, PII only in redacted form (rest-REQ-016).
Keep probe traffic out of info-level logs and endpoint RED series (rest-REQ-006).
internalStructure: A request-telemetry context created by the pipeline's edge middleware and enriched as the request progresses; log, metric, and span emitters read the same context so field values never disagree across signals.

interfaces.name: telemetry context
interfaces.description: Request id, trace context, auth class, path template, and timing, shared by all three emitters.

interfaces.name: signal exporters
interfaces.description: Where logs, metrics, and traces go is deployment configuration; the shapes emitted are contract.

dependencies.name: Request pipeline
dependencies.description: The pipeline creates and finalises the telemetry context per request.

tradeoffs: One shared context adds a small per-request allocation and buys signal agreement: the duration in the log line, the histogram sample, and the span timing come from the same clock reads. Emitting three signals is redundant by design; each answers a question the others answer badly.
